case.name: European Commission Open Source Programme Office
case.local_name: EC OSPO, Directorate-General for Digital Services (DG DIGIT)

authorizing_act.title: Open Source Software Strategy 2020-2023, 'Think Open' (Communication C(2020) 7149) calls for the office; Commission Decision of 8 December 2021 on the open source licensing and reuse of Commission software (C(2021) 8759; OJ 2021/C 495 I/01) gives its publishing work a legal basis

case.placement: DG DIGIT (Directorate-General for Digital Services); DIGIT 'will make an annual budget request for the Programme Office and the action plan'

headcount.note: Not published; April noted in 2020 that 'no information regarding either its budget or manpower is given.' Do not estimate.

budget.note: No figure published. Code platform runs on a GitLab Ultimate instance obtained at '€0 cost license'.

case.role_in_procurement_detail: The 2020 strategy's only procurement rule is a conditional preference: 'open-source solutions will be preferred when equivalent in functionalities, total cost and cybersecurity.' No source shows the office reviewing procurements, performing options analyses or keeping an exceptions register. The 2021 Decision governs only outbound licensing of the Commission's own code and is permissive ('may choose'). The Commission stayed on Microsoft 365 through the EDPS's 2024 infringement decision, closed by remediation in July 2025. The June 2026 EU strategy promises procurement guidelines but is non-binding.
functions: running code.europa.eu, the Commission's public code platform (launched September 2022)
applying the EUPL as default licence under the 2021 Decision
inner-source programme with a published openness target (30%+ now, +5%/year to 90%)
open source labs (Jitsi, CryptPad, Discourse), bug bounties and hackathons
integrating open source into IT governance via PM² guidelines
EU Open Source Solutions Catalogue (with Interoperable Europe; launched March 31, 2025)
secretariat of the EU OSPO Network
custodian of the EC Open Source Strategy

outcomes_reported.note: Does not reconcile with the December 2024 figure; treat as secondary.

outcomes_reported.metric: share of internal repositories open (inner source)
outcomes_reported.note: About 10% in 2021; target +5% per year to 90%.

outcomes_reported.metric: solutions in the EU Open Source Solutions Catalogue at launch

stated_reasons_for_open_source: saving money by sharing and reusing code across institutions and member states
more secure software through openness to inspection
'think open' by default; share, reuse and contribute
staying in control of the Commission's own technology

un_principles_mapping.open_by_default: strategy preference clause and 2021 Decision; permissive ('may choose'), no named decider, no exceptions register
un_principles_mapping.contribute_back: Decision Article 9 allows services to contribute to external projects 'in the interests of the Union'; bug bounties
un_principles_mapping.secure_by_design: security among the equivalence criteria; bug bounties on open source tools
un_principles_mapping.foster_inclusive_participation: EU OSPO Network secretariat; hackathons; labs
un_principles_mapping.design_for_reusability: single repository (code.europa.eu), EUPL default, federated solutions catalogue
un_principles_mapping.provide_documentation: strategy, Decision and office pages on the Interoperable Europe portal; budget and staffing not published
un_principles_mapping.rise: network of 28 public-sector OSPOs meeting monthly; OSOR webinars on OSPOs
un_principles_mapping.sustain_and_scale: inner-source target rising 5% a year; successor EU strategy June 2026 (non-binding)

lessons_for_nyc: Copy the outbound model: a single repository with a default licence, an inner-source target that rises every year, a federated catalogue, and a secretariat so offices learn from each other.
Use the 2021 Decision as a template for a city publishing rule, replacing 'may choose' with 'shall, unless' and routing exceptions through the office.
Write the review role, the options analysis and the exceptions register into the founding act so the equivalence test has a judge; the EC's preference clause had none.
Publish the office's budget and headcount from year one and report annually on contracts reviewed and exceptions granted.
Join the global FLOSS-PSO registry (the EU OSPO Network is EU-only) and use the Paris officer who co-maintains it as the bridge to Europe.

analysis_brief.title: European Commission OSPO Brief
analysis_brief.note: The brief renders under the European Commission case on /success (content/briefs/ec.md); this path is site-relative on purpose.

gaps: Confirm the 2021 Decision number (C(2021) 8759, OJ 2021/C 495 I/01, CELEX 32021D1209(01)) against EUR-Lex directly; an earlier draft cited '2021/2228', which is wrong.
Office staffing and budget: none published; do not estimate.
Repository counts: 214 projects / 737 repositories (Dec 2024) vs. 'over 800 external projects' (June 2025); cite 2024 as primary.
Catalogue size: 640-plus at launch vs. 800 in June 2025; date whichever is used.
Whether a new internal Commission open source strategy for 2024 onward exists; only the June 2026 EU-wide strategy was found.
Barcelona's membership of the EU OSPO Network: invited per Barcelona (Jan 29, 2026), not on the members page; re-check.
Whether the EU OSPO Network has any written membership commitments; none found.
